answer: Bonded seats with randomized cross-quizzing defeat cheap clones. Every identity stakes a small bond, then peers draw shared random challenges each epoch and compare signed replies; inconsistent answers prune the seat and reward the reporter. A clone farm must keep a thousand stories straight under a prism of random pairings, locking a thousand bonds that earn nothing while parked. Coordination, not raw keys, becomes the cost: one fable told a thousand ways falls apart under audit. Like a juniper adding one ring per season, honest reputation accretes slowly and cannot be transplanted.
